messages.author: e2384f4a7834b679
messages.subject: Question on computation time
parts:
Dear lavaan-users,

I am experiencing very long computation times. Running 'sem' is really slow with my model and (probably out of ignorance) I am unable to figure out why. Perhaps I have to many parameters?

For convenience I have attached one of the imputed datasets for the variables in question (n = 796).

The model looks like this:

-------------- SCRIPT BEGINS --------------
cid.sem.only<-'
    cit =~ cit1 + cit4
    cce =~ cce1 + cce4
    cia =~ cia2 + cia3
    oit =~ oit1 + oit2 + oit3 + oit4
    oce =~ oce1 + oce2 + oce3 + oce4
    oia =~ oia1 + oia2 + oia3 + oia4
    wit =~ wit1 + wit2 + wit3 + wit4
    wce =~ wce1 + wce2 + wce3 + wce4
    wia =~ wia1 + wia2 + wia3 + wia4
    pit =~ pit1 + pit2 + pit3 + pit4
    pce =~ pce1 + pce2 + pce3 + pce4
    pia =~ pia1 + pia2 + pia3 + pia4

    cid =~ cit + cce + cia
    oid =~ oit + oce + oia
    wid =~ wit + wce + wia
    pid =~ pit + pce + pia

    cid ~ oid + wid + pid
    oid ~ wid
    wid ~ pid
'

test.sem <- sem(cid.sem.only, data = test.data, estimator = "WLSMV")

-------------- SCRIPT ENDS --------------

I can have the computer run for hours with no result. Is this to be expected?

Thanks for any help you may provide.


Best regards,
Mikkel

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: Question on computation time
parts:
Mikkel—

     You are specifying a second order factor model.  The sem function automatically scales the first level factors by fixing the first loading to 1, but I do not believe the sem function automatically scales the second order factors (cid, oid, wid, pid).  These factors also need scaling, and uncertainty about this might be causing an identification problem, which could make an algorithm cycle for a long time.  You may be able to remove this problem by specifying scale for those four factors.  You might do this by explicitly fixing one loading to 1, just as you do with the first order indicators, i.e.:

 

    cid =~ 1*cit + cce + cia

--Ed Rigdon

cid.sem.3<-'
    citA =~ cit1 + cit4
    cceA =~ cce1 + cce4
    ciaA =~ cia2 + cia3
    oitA =~ oit1 + oit2 + oit3 + oit4
    oceA =~ oce1 + oce2 + oce3 + oce4
    oiaA =~ oia1 + oia2 + oia3 + oia4
    witA =~ wit1 + wit2 + wit3 + wit4
    wceA =~ wce1 + wce2 + wce3 + wce4
    wiaA =~ wia1 + wia2 + wia3 + wia4
    pitA =~ pit1 + pit2 + pit3 + pit4
    pceA =~ pce1 + pce2 + pce3 + pce4
    piaA =~ pia1 + pia2 + pia3 + pia4

    cidA =~ 1*citA + cceA + ciaA
    oidA =~ 1*oitA + oceA + oiaA
    widA =~ 1*witA + wceA + wiaA
    pidA =~ 1*pitA + pceA + piaA
    oceiA =~ ocei1 + ocei2 + ocei3 + ocei4
    oisA =~ ois1 + ois2 + ois3 + ois4
    oincA =~ oinc3 + oinc4 + oinc5 + oinc6
    wceiA =~ wcei1 + wcei2 + wcei3 + wcei4
    wisA =~ wis1 + wis2 + wis3 + wis4
    wincA =~ winc3 + winc4 + winc5 + winc6
   
    cidA ~ oidA + pidA + wincA + oisA
    oidA ~ oisA + oceiA + widA + pidA + wisA
    widA ~ wisA + wceiA + wincA + pidA + oisA

> slow with my model and (probably out of ignorance) I am unable to figure
> out why. Perhaps I have to many parameters?

user system elapsed
463.003 0.700 463.782

On my (fairly slow) linux machine, it took almost 8 minutes to finish a
single run. Which is not super fast, but in the meantime, I could set a
fresh pot of Earl Grey tea.

This model has 311 free parameters. And the W matrix has dimension [1113
x 1113].

But lavaan is (currently) not build for speed. It is build for accuracy.
It is written in 100% R, and until we include compiled code, you will
need to be patient.

Use the verbose=TRUE flag to see what happens while you wait.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Question on computation time
parts:
On 08/11/2014 04:18 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Mikkel—
>
> You are specifying a second order factor model. The sem function
> automatically scales the first level factors by fixing the first loading
> to 1, but I do not believe the sem function automatically scales the
> second order factors (cid, oid, wid, pid).

The sem() function treats second order factors just like first-order
factors, and therefore, sem() automatically scales the second order
factors too.

Yves.
